title: Animation Microcredential Curriculum Framework, Rationale, and Three-Course Syllabus Design (Animation I–III)
goal: Develop a new three-course Animation curriculum in film (Animation I, II, and III) and create a complete Animation Microcredential proposal suitable for departmental and curriculum committee review.
occupation: Chair and associate professor in the department of theater and film

session_goal_achievement.Why or why not: I was able to get the outline of three courses as well as the justification for the microcredential from the hour’s work.

Step-1 + Step-5.step_name: Develop and Position the Animation Microcredential
Step-1 + Step-5.step_action: Develop an animation microcredential aligned with the film program's overall goals by reviewing program outcomes, industry expectations for beginning animators, instructional scaffolding and differentiation, and the progression across the three animation courses. Organize the resulting curriculum into a coherent and marketable microcredential suitable for curriculum committee review, including its purpose, learning outcomes, implementation strategy, target audiences, and relationship to the film major as a whole.

nodes.label: Define the microcredential framework task and Claude's instructional-designer role
nodes.detail: The participant opens a new Claude project and types a prompt establishing that she is building an animation framework for a microcredential housed in the film major, and that Claude should act as an instructional designer working alongside her.

nodes.label: Elicit the microcredential's overall goal and inter-course sequencing logic
nodes.detail: Claude asks structured, multiple-choice-style questions to pin down what a learner should be able to do after all three courses, how Animation I/II/III relate sequentially (both entry points, III requiring both as prerequisites), and the course format (3-credit, 15-week).

nodes.label: Retrieve and review the film program's institutional goals document
nodes.detail: She signs into Microsoft OneDrive, locates the 'Film Program Goals' document, and reviews it to ground the framework in the department's existing outcomes before continuing with Claude.

nodes.label: Provide curriculum goals, course structure, and instructional-design guidance
Develop course outcomes and verify PLO alignment across the microcredential
nodes.detail: Using the user's clarified goals, sequencing, course structure, and instructional guidance, Claude develops course-level outcomes across Animation I, II, and III, then checks the resulting CLOs against the film program's four PLOs across the Introductory/Developing/Mastery tiers. It flags two coverage gaps involving PLO3's small-team leadership expectation and PLO4's critical/historical context.

nodes.label: Review the drafted animation microcredential curriculum framework
Resolve the flagged PLO gaps as intentionally covered elsewhere
nodes.detail: The user decides both flagged gaps should be left as-is: PLO3 team leadership is covered by other film production courses, and PLO4's critical/historical analysis is intentionally deferred to FLM 400/499.

nodes.label: Compile the curriculum framework into a formal draft document
nodes.detail: Claude assembles a Program Overview, a PLO Alignment Matrix, and course-level outcomes/assessment sections for all three courses into a Word document titled 'Animation Microcredential — Curriculum Framework — Draft.'
nodes.softwares: Claude (desktop app, docx skill), Microsoft Word

nodes.label: Review the compiled animation microcredential curriculum framework
Define the microcredential's proposal positioning and institutional rationale
nodes.detail: The user asks Claude to articulate why the curriculum should function as a cross-disciplinary microcredential rather than a three-course sequence within the film major, identifying potential audiences in Computer Science, Digital Media/Communications, and students interested in animation. Through Claude's follow-up questions, the user selects cross-disciplinary market demand as the core institutional rationale and confirms the audience-specific value propositions.

nodes.label: Draft the rationale document arguing cross-disciplinary demand and structural fit
nodes.detail: Using the user's proposal framing and responses to its follow-up questions, Claude writes 'Rationale: Animation as a Microcredential, Not a Major Track — Prepared for Curriculum Committee Review,' covering cross-disciplinary demand, audience-specific value, structural fit, and the rationale for offering the curriculum as a microcredential rather than a film-major course sequence.
nodes.softwares: Claude (desktop app, docx skill), Microsoft Word

nodes.label: Review the drafted microcredential rationale
Request labor-market and peer-institution data to substantiate the rationale
nodes.detail: The user asks Claude to show labor-market and peer-institution data that can back up the cross-disciplinary demand argument.

nodes.label: Research and incorporate supporting evidence into the microcredential rationale
nodes.detail: Claude researches labor-market statistics and peer-institution microcredential programs using sources including the Bureau of Labor Statistics, the Entertainment Software Association, and examples from peer institutions, then incorporates the findings and cited sources into a Supporting Data section of the rationale document.
nodes.softwares: Claude (desktop app, Web Search connector), Microsoft Word

nodes.label: Review the evidence-supported microcredential rationale

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source a10: Requests a rationale for offering the curriculum as a cross disciplinary microcredential.
Target a14: Outputs the Rationale doc 
Reasoning: a11 drafts it, a13 asks for supporting evidence, user accepts a14.

Step-2.step_name: Write class syllabus and calendar for Animation I
Step-2.step_action: Use Claude to build a syllabus that includes syllabi requirements of my institution and also builds engaging projects using the software available to students.

nodes.label: Specify Animation I's calendar and unit progression
nodes.detail: The user states the Animation I semester dates (Aug 19–Dec 1, Tuesday/Thursday 11:15–12:30, Thanksgiving week off) and the intended unit progression: flipbooks, then rotoscoping, then stop motion, then 2D character rigging in Photoshop as a bridge to Animation II.

nodes.label: Clarify session allocation and grading for Animation I
nodes.detail: Claude clarifies how the available class sessions should be allocated across the four technique units and how each unit's short sequence should be graded.

nodes.label: Review the evidence-supported microcredential rationale
Answer Claude's clarifying questions
nodes.detail: User answers clarifying questions.

nodes.label: Develop the full 28-session Animation I syllabus
nodes.detail: Uses the user's responses to develop the full 28-session syllabus. The syllabus progresses through flipbooks, rotoscoping, stop motion, and 2D rigging, anchors each unit to a historical animation example, and concludes with a three-week final project.
nodes.softwares: Claude (desktop app, docx skill), Microsoft Word

nodes.label: Review the completed Animation I syllabus
nodes.detail: The user reviews the finished 'Animation I: Foundations (Analog)' syllabus, including its course description, course-level outcomes, and grading breakdown table.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source b1: Requests the Animation I syllabus 
Target b5: Outputs Animation I syllabus.
Reasoning: User accepts b5 without further modifications.

Step-3.step_action: Use Claude to build a syllabus for a class that builds on Animation I while pushing students into higher levels of achievement. Maintain curricular continuity with assignments of increasing difficulty.

nodes.label: Specify Animation II as a hybrid, character-building course building on Animation I
nodes.detail: The user directs Claude to build Animation II next, assuming the same class structure and timeframe but as a hybrid course with online lectures/instruction and in-class time devoted entirely to building and rigging a character in Blender and Maya.

nodes.label: Clarify Animation II's course structure
nodes.detail: Claude clarifies the course structure with the user, establishing a single sustained character-building pipeline across the semester, parallel introductory treatment of Blender and Maya before students commit to one, and a hybrid format with online lecture/tutorial content and in-class hands-on studio work.

nodes.label: Answer Claude's clarifying questions
nodes.detail: User answers clarifying questions.

nodes.label: Develop the Animation II hybrid character-building syllabus
nodes.detail: Using these decisions, Claude develops 'Animation II: Digital Character Building,' with course-level outcomes for a complete 3D character workflow and checkpoint-based grading across concept development, modeling, texturing/shading, rigging, and the final character build.
nodes.softwares: Claude (desktop app, docx skill), Microsoft Word

nodes.label: Review Claude's Animation II syllabus response

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source c1: USer requests Animation II syllabus
Target c4: Outputs the Animation II
Reasoning: User accepts c4 without any modifications

Step-4.step_action: Use Claude to build the final animation course in the sequence emphasizing a completed film. The work should build a class with a sophisticated project at the end.

nodes.label: Issue a combined instruction to build Animation III and then realign the whole proposal
nodes.detail: While Claude is still finishing Animation II, the user pre-types a detailed Animation III spec (sizzle-reel capstone, incubator model, weekly notes as a grade item) and appends 'Once you build the Animation III class, analyze and realign the microcredential, making adjustments as necessary to the microcredential proposal,' then sends it as one combined instruction.

nodes.label: Develop the Animation III sizzle-reel capstone syllabus (Interrupted)
nodes.detail: Claude begins working on Animation III syllabus, but hits an error. (The user waits, then stops the generation (d4))
nodes.softwares: Claude (desktop app, docx skill), Microsoft Word

nodes.label: Check all generated files
Wait and stop the generation
Resubmit the Animation III syllabus requirements after the interrupted attempt
Clarify whether the original team-based phase should remain in Animation III
nodes.detail: Claude clarifies the Animation III capstone structure with the user, establishing individual project development with peer critique, a condensed narrative short or trailer as the sizzle-reel format, and a reel-plus-pitch-package final deliverable with weekly pitch-and-notes checkpoints.

nodes.label: Answer Claude's clarifying questions
nodes.detail: User answers Claude's clarifying questions.

nodes.label: Develop the Animation III syllabus
nodes.detail: Using these decisions, Claude develops 'Animation III: Pitch Incubator & Sizzle Reel,' with course-level outcomes centered on producing and iterating an original animated project and a grading structure that emphasizes the final sizzle reel and pitch package.
nodes.softwares: Claude (desktop app, docx skill), Microsoft Word

Step-1.step_name: Align the animation curriculum framework to the film program's overall goals.
Step-1.step_action: Review the goals, consider industry expectations for beginning animators, and how the three classes work together to present a complete animation credential. Review goals in terms of scaffolding of instruction as well as differentiation of instruction.

nodes.label: Request an alignment check between the built courses and the microcredential proposal
nodes.detail: With all three syllabi now built, the user explicitly asks Claude to analyze the three courses and determine whether they still align with the microcredential proposal, prompting a fresh review of the original framework document.

nodes.label: Analyze course alignment and identify needed updates to the microcredential framework
nodes.detail: Claude reviews the original Curriculum Framework against the three completed syllabi and identifies misalignment caused by Animation III's shift from a team-built shared-world model to an individual pitch-incubator model, particularly in the framework's PLO3 and PLO4 justifications. Claude concludes that the as-built courses support the PLO1/PLO2 mastery claims but recommends updating the framework to reflect the revised course designs and asks the user whether to make those changes.

nodes.label: Review the completed Animation III syllabus
nodes.detail: The user reviews the finished Animation III syllabus, its learning outcomes, and its timeline.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source d1: Requests Animation III syllabus
Target d8: Outputs the Animation III syllabus.
Reasoning: User reviews and accepts the finished syllabus Animation III

nodes.label: Review Claude's course-to-framework alignment analysis
Approve updating the curriculum framework document
nodes.detail: The user confirms with 'YES,' authorizing Claude to revise the framework document rather than the built syllabi.

nodes.label: Revise the framework document's stale descriptions and PLO mechanisms
nodes.detail: Claude reads its own build script, then updates Animation I's stale course description, Animation II's CLO/pipeline text, and rewrites the full Animation III section of the framework document, building and verifying the file; the session ends here without assembling the final combined microcredential proposal document.

nodes.label: Review the revised animation microcredential curriculum framework

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source a1: User requests an animation microcredential framework, with Claude as instructional designer.
Target e6: Outputs the revised Curriculum Framework document, aligned to the built 3 animation courses.
Reasoning: a8 drafts it, d1 and e1 ask to realign after the courses change, e5 confirms Claude's suggetion; user reviews e6 and accepts.
